_policy: HAND-WRITTEN. No upstream response. All identities fictional; see README.md.
_shape: Roster records as `sansad.ingest.members.load_members` reads them. `lsExpr` is the comma-separated enumeration of every Lok Sabha a member served in, which is what the real roster serves and what T086's window filter reads.

_cases.fx-c001 / fx-c002: Constituency Theta, State Alpha -- TWO DIFFERENT HOLDERS across the covered terms (17 then 18). US3 acceptance scenario 3.
_cases.fx-c003: Constituency Iota, State Alpha -- ONE member holding BOTH covered terms. Must produce TWO representations, not one; this is the case the old (member_id, start_date) key collapsed, and it is the majority case in the real data (216 of 545 seats).
_cases.fx-c004: Constituency Kappa, State Alpha -- a holder in the 17th only; the seat has no 18th-term representation at all.
_cases.fx-c005: Constituency Theta, State BETA -- the SAME SEAT NAME in a different state. Must be a separate row with its own state, never merged with fx-c001/fx-c002.
_cases.fx-c006: Constituency Lambda, State Gamma -- terms 15 and 16 ONLY, both outside the covered window. The seat must not appear in the set at all.
_cases.fx-c007: Constituency Mu, State Gamma -- terms 16 AND 17: the out-of-window term is dropped and the in-window one kept, on one member.
_cases.fx-c008: State Delta -- the seat carries the state's own name, so the id's two halves are one slug and are not repeated.
_cases.fx-c009: Constituency Nu, State Alpha -- party and state recorded as empty, so the published row must carry an explicit 'not stated' rather than a blank.
